new.name: Tabory Snake Fly
new.description: A long, snaking saltwater-and-trout streamer: a long ostrich or marabou tail and a spun deer hair collar and head that pushes water.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly across currents at night for stripers, or for big trout in rivers.
mats: Long ostrich herl or marabou with a few flash strands
steps: Tie a long, sparse tail with a little flash.
Spin a deer hair collar, leaving the tips facing back.
Spin more hair in front and trim it to a round head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Henryville Special
new.description: A classic Pennsylvania caddis: green floss body palmered with grizzly, a wood duck underwing, grey duck quill wings tented on top and a brown hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the evening during caddis hatches; it floats low and looks buggy.
steps: Tie in the grizzly hackle and floss at the bend.
Wrap the floss body and palmer the hackle; trim it on top.
Tie a short wood duck underwing and two duck quill slips tented over it.
Wind a brown collar and whip finish.

new.name: Ally's Shrimp
new.description: Perhaps the most popular modern salmon fly: a long orange bucktail tail, a red and black floss body ribbed with oval tinsel, a grey squirrel underwing, golden pheasant tippet back and an orange collar.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on a floating or intermediate line through salmon pools in summer.
steps: Tie in a long orange bucktail tail and the rib.
Wrap red floss over the rear half and black over the front; rib it.
Tie grey squirrel under and over the body, then a golden pheasant tippet on top.
Wind an orange collar, sweep it back and finish with a red head.

new.name: Killer Bug
new.description: Sawyer's grayling bug: copper wire underbody covered with Chadwick's 477 wool or a pinkish-grey substitute. Nothing else, and deadly.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in winter for grayling and trout, letting it drop then lifting it.
mats: Chadwick's 477 wool or a fawn-pink substitute
steps: Wrap copper wire to build a hump at the front and back of the shank.
Tie in the wool with the wire and wrap a plump, cigar-shaped body.
Lock it off with a few turns of wire at the eye.

new.name: Pink Lady
new.description: A bright attractor dry: pink floss body ribbed with gold, a ginger tail and hackle and grey duck wings.
new.fishing_tips: Use it as an attractor on summer streams.
new.creator_name: Classic American dry (George La Branche era)
steps: Tie in the wings upright and divided.
Add the tail and the rib.
Wrap a pink floss body and rib it.
Wind the ginger hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Black Gnat
new.description: A simple black dry: black hackle fibre tail, black dubbed or herl body, grey wing and black hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it when small dark flies are on the water, or as a general summer dry.
mats: Grey duck quill or white Antron
steps: Tie in a black tail.
Dub a slim black body.
Tie in a small wing.
Wind the black hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Yellow May Dun
new.description: A pale yellow dun: yellow tail, yellow dubbed body and a yellow-dyed hackle, sometimes with CDC wings.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in May and June on British rivers when the yellow mayflies hatch.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Dub a slim yellow body.
Tie in the wing upright.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Grey Duster
new.description: A shaggy, all-purpose dry: a light blue rabbit fur body and a badger hackle. Suggests many duns and spinners.
new.fishing_tips: A great general dry on rivers and lakes all season.
steps: Tie in a short tail if you like.
Dub a tapered body.
Wind a badger hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Kite's Imperial
new.description: A dun pattern for olives: honey dun tail, a purple silk body ribbed with gold wire with a heron herl thorax, and a honey dun hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during olive hatches, especially in spring and autumn.
mats: Grey heron herl (or substitute) over purple silk
steps: Tie in the tail and wire.
Wind the herl body, doubling it up at the thorax, and rib it.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Blue Upright
new.description: A simple Devon dry: stripped peacock quill body, blue dun tail and hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Use it on fast moorland streams when olives are about.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the stripped quill body.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Leadwing Coachman
new.description: A peacock herl body with a gold tag, a brown hackle and slate grey duck wings.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it through riffles in the evening; suggests Isonychia nymphs and caddis.
steps: Tie a small gold tag.
Wind a full peacock herl body.
Tie a brown beard.
Tie in the wing slips and whip finish.

new.name: Coachman
new.description: The original Coachman: peacock herl body, white duck wings and a brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as an evening attractor; the white wing is easy to see.
steps: Tie in the wings.
Wind a peacock herl body.
Wind the brown hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Hare's Ear Wet Fly
new.description: A rough hare's ear body ribbed with gold, picked out for legs, under a grey duck wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film or just under during olive and sedge hatches.
steps: Tie in a short tail and the rib.
Dub a rough body and rib it.
Pick out the thorax fibres as legs.
Tie in a low wing and whip finish.

new.name: Partridge and Yellow
new.description: A North Country spider: a yellow silk body and a sparse grey partridge hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish a team of spiders across and down, or upstream, in spring.
steps: Wrap a slim yellow silk body.
Add a tiny thorax if you like.
Wind one or two turns of partridge and finish.

new.name: Snipe and Purple
new.description: A purple silk body with a snipe hackle: one of the best early-season spider patterns.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in cold spring water when iron blue duns hatch.
steps: Wrap a slim purple silk body.
Wind one or two turns of snipe hackle and finish.

new.name: Waterhen Bloa
new.description: A yellow silk body lightly dubbed with mole fur and a waterhen (moorhen) underwing hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A top early-season fly for olive hatches.
steps: Dub mole fur thinly so the silk shows through.
Wind a sparse waterhen hackle and finish.

new.name: Greenwell's Spider
new.description: Waxed yellow silk ribbed with gold wire and a soft Greenwell hen hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it upstream or across in riffles during olive hatches.
steps: Wrap a slim waxed silk body and rib it.
Wind a sparse hen hackle and finish.

new.name: Black Spider
new.description: Stewart's famous spider: brown silk body and a black (cock starling) hackle palmered short.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it upstream, Stewart style, in summer.
steps: Wrap a slim silk body.
Wind a sparse hackle and finish.

new.name: Woodcock and Hare's Ear
new.description: A hare's ear body ribbed with gold under a woodcock wing.
new.fishing_tips: A great sedge and olive suggestion for loughs and rivers.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub the body and rib it.
Add a beard hackle and the wing, whip finish.

new.name: Silver Invicta
new.description: The Invicta with a silver body: golden pheasant crest tail, silver tinsel body palmered with red game, blue jay throat and hen pheasant wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for sea trout and for lake trout feeding on fry.
steps: Tie in the tail, wire and hackle.
Wrap the silver body, palmer the hackle and rib it.
Add the jay throat and the wing, whip finish.

new.name: Kingfisher Butcher
new.description: A Butcher variant: gold body, kingfisher blue tail, orange hackle and a blue mallard wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on loch drifts and for sea trout.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the gold body.
Add the orange beard and the wing, whip finish.

new.name: Butcher
new.description: Red tail, flat silver body, black hackle and blue mallard wing; a classic fry and attractor fly.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the point for trout and sea trout.
steps: Tie in the red tail.
Wrap the silver body.
Add the black beard and the wing, whip finish.

new.name: Bloody Butcher
new.description: The Butcher with a red hackle instead of black.
new.fishing_tips: A loch and reservoir classic, especially in coloured water.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the silver body.
Add the red beard and the wing, whip finish.

new.name: Mallard and Claret
new.description: A claret seal fur body ribbed with gold, a golden pheasant tippet tail, claret hackle and bronze mallard wing.
new.fishing_tips: One of the best loch and sea trout flies, especially on dull days.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub the claret body and rib it.
Add the hackle and a rolled mallard wing, whip finish.

new.name: Teal Blue and Silver
new.description: Golden pheasant tippet tail, flat silver body ribbed with wire, blue hackle and teal flank wing.
new.fishing_tips: A top sea trout fly at night and a good fry imitation in lakes.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Wrap the silver body and rib it.
Add the blue beard and teal wing, whip finish.

new.name: Connemara Black
new.description: Black seal fur body with an oval silver rib, golden pheasant crest tail, black hackle with a blue jay throat and bronze mallard wing.
new.fishing_tips: A great Irish lough fly in a good wave, and for sea trout.
mats: Black hen with blue jay in front
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub the body and rib it.
Wind the black hackle and a turn of jay.
Tie in the mallard wing and whip finish.

new.name: Bibio
new.description: A black seal fur body with a red band in the middle, ribbed with silver and palmered with black hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A top dropper on Irish loughs, especially when heather flies are about.
mats: Black seal fur, red seal fur, black seal fur
steps: Tie in the rib and hackle.
Dub black, a band of red, then black.
Palmer the hackle and rib it, whip finish.

new.name: Kate McLaren
new.description: A palmered black fly: golden pheasant crest tail, black seal fur body ribbed with silver, a black body hackle and a red game hackle at the front.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the top dropper in a wave for trout and sea trout.
steps: Tie in the tail, rib and black hackle.
Dub the body, palmer and rib it.
Wind a red game hackle at the front, whip finish.

new.name: Clan Chief
new.description: A loch dropper fly: red and yellow wool tail, black seal fur body ribbed with silver, red and black hackles palmered and a black front hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the top dropper for trout and sea trout in a big wave.
mats: Red and black cock, palmered together
steps: Tie in the tail, rib and two body hackles.
Dub the body, palmer both hackles and rib them.
Wind a black front hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Sooty Olive
new.description: A dark olive seal fur body ribbed with gold, golden pheasant tippet tail, black hackle and bronze mallard wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during olive and buzzer hatches on Irish loughs.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub and rib the body.
Add the hackle and wing, whip finish.

new.name: Claret Bumble
new.description: A Kingsmill Moore bumble: claret seal fur, golden pheasant tippet tail, black and claret hackles palmered with a blue jay collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the top dropper in a wave on Irish loughs.
steps: Tie in the tail, rib and the two hackles.
Dub the body, palmer the hackles and rib them.
Wind a jay collar and whip finish.

new.name: Shipman's Buzzer
new.description: A floating buzzer: seal fur body ribbed with pearl and white Antron tufts at the tail and head that keep it in the film.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it static in the film when buzzers are hatching on stillwaters.
steps: Tie in a white tuft at the tail and the rib.
Dub the body and rib it.
Tie in a white tuft at the eye, trim both short and whip finish.

new.name: Booby
new.description: A buoyant lure with foam eyes and a marabou tail, fished on a fast-sinking line so it hovers above the bottom.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a short leader with a sinking line and a very slow retrieve.
mats: Foam booby eyes in stocking mesh or foam cylinder
steps: Tie the foam eyes on firmly with figure-eight wraps.
Tie in a marabou tail.
Wrap a fritz body up to the eyes and whip finish.

new.name: Blob
new.description: A ball of bright fritz with a small tail: simple, bright and very effective on stocked rainbows.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast or hang it on a sinking line.
mats: Fritz or Blob chenille, wrapped fat
steps: Tie in the fritz.
Wrap it into a round ball, stroking the fibres back.
Whip finish.

new.name: Cat's Whisker
new.description: A white marabou lure with a white chenille body, bead chain eyes and a white marabou wing.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it on stillwaters; one of the best lures for stocked rainbows.
steps: Tie in the bead chain eyes and a marabou tail.
Wrap a chenille body.
Tie a marabou wing on top, whip finish.

new.name: Damsel Booby
new.description: A booby in damsel olive: foam eyes, olive marabou tail and a dubbed olive body.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slow on a sinking line around weedbeds in summer.
steps: Tie the foam eyes on.
Add the marabou tail.
Dub a slim body, rib it and whip finish.

new.name: Fritz Lure
new.description: A marabou tail and a wrapped fritz body: quick to tie and colourful.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it on a floating or sinking line for rainbows.
steps: Tie in a marabou tail.
Wrap the fritz forward.
Whip finish.

new.name: Humungus
new.description: A big, bright lure: marabou tail, fritz or chenille body and a large gold bead or cone head.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast through stocked fisheries.
steps: Add the bead.
Tie in the marabou tail.
Wrap the fritz and whip finish.

new.name: Minkie
new.description: A mink zonker strip lure with a pearl body and a bead head; a big, breathing fry imitation.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it around fry-bashing trout in autumn.
steps: Add the bead and wrap a pearl body.
Tie a mink strip along the top, Matuka style or just at the head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Montana Nymph
new.description: A black stonefly nymph: black hackle tips tail, black chenille abdomen and a yellow chenille thorax with a black hackle and black chenille wing case.
new.fishing_tips: Strip or dead-drift it; also a top stillwater pattern in the UK.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap a black chenille abdomen.
Tie in the wing case chenille and hackle, wrap a yellow thorax and palmer the hackle.
Pull the wing case over and whip finish.

new.name: Montana Stone
new.description: A bigger, weighted western stonefly: goose biot tails, black chenille body with a yellow belly and a heavy hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it deep through riffles.
steps: Weight the hook and tie in split biot tails.
Wrap a black abdomen.
Wrap a yellow thorax with a palmered hackle under a black wing case.
Whip finish.

new.name: Orange Blob
new.description: The classic orange version of the Blob.
new.fishing_tips: Pull it fast through stocked rainbows in summer.
steps: Tie in the fritz.
Wrap a round ball.
Whip finish.

new.name: Coch-y-Bonddu
new.description: A beetle pattern: a gold tag, peacock herl body and a coch-y-bonddu (red-black) hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in summer when beetles fall on the water.
steps: Tie a small gold tag.
Wind a fat herl body.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Lime Trude
new.description: A bright attractor: golden pheasant tippet tail, lime green dubbed body, white calf hair downwing and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A great attractor for pocket water and as a dry-dropper indicator.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Dub a lime body.
Tie a calf hair downwing.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Royal Trude
new.description: Royal Coachman colours with a white calf hair downwing: easy to tie and see.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in fast mountain water.
mats: Peacock herl with a red floss band
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wind herl, red floss, herl.
Add the calf hair wing.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Coachman Trude
new.description: Peacock herl body, white calf downwing and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: An attractor for broken water.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wind a herl body.
Add the wing.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Turck's Tarantula
new.description: A spun deer hair head and collar, rubber legs, a white calf hair wing over an amber body: a hopper, stonefly and cicada suggestion.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it along banks in summer.
mats: White calf body hair with flash
steps: Tie in the tail and dub the body.
Tie in the wing.
Spin deer hair for the collar and head, add legs each side.
Trim the head and whip finish.

new.name: Club Sandwich
new.description: A layered foam terrestrial with rubber legs and a sighter, floating high in rough water.
new.fishing_tips: A strong dry-dropper indicator and hopper.
mats: Two layers of 2mm foam with a dubbed underbody
steps: Glue two foam colours together and cut a body.
Lash it down along the shank over dubbing.
Add wing, legs and sighter at the front tie-in point.
Whip finish.

new.name: Charlie Boy Hopper
new.description: A simple foam hopper: one strip of foam folded over the shank, a sparkle wing and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Quick to tie; great as an indicator for a nymph dropper.
steps: Tie the foam along the shank in two segments.
Add the wing at the front segment.
Add legs and the sighter, whip finish.

new.name: Hippie Stomper
new.description: A small foam attractor with a flashy dubbed body, white wing post and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a summer attractor and dry-dropper float.
steps: Tie in the tail and foam strip.
Dub the body and pull the foam over.
Add the wing and legs at the tie-down point.
Whip finish.

new.name: Gypsy King
new.description: A buggy foam terrestrial with a dubbed body, deer hair wing and a foam head, imitating hoppers and big stoneflies.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it tight to banks.
steps: Lash the foam body over dubbing.
Tie in an elk wing.
Add legs, fold the foam forward for a head and whip finish.

new.name: Chubby Chernobyl
new.description: A foam terrestrial with an Ice Dub body, a fluffy synthetic wing and plenty of rubber legs; floats forever.
new.fishing_tips: The go-to dry-dropper float in the West.
steps: Dub the body.
Tie the foam on top at the front and rear.
Add the wing and legs at the front tie-in.
Whip finish.

new.name: Pool Toy Hopper
new.description: A multi-layer foam hopper with long rubber legs, a sighter and a synthetic wing.
new.fishing_tips: Hold big droppers in rough water.
steps: Cut and lash the foam body in segments.
Add the wing.
Add legs and sighter, whip finish.

new.name: Thunder Thighs Hopper
new.description: A foam hopper with big, kicking back legs made from knotted foam or rubber.
new.fishing_tips: Plop it along banks in late summer.
steps: Lash the foam body down.
Tie in the wing.
Attach the back legs and front legs, whip finish.

new.name: Joe's Hopper
new.description: A classic hopper: red tail, yellow chenille body palmered with brown, turkey wings and a grizzly and brown hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it along grassy banks in late summer.
mats: Yellow chenille with a loop over the tail
steps: Tie in the tail and a small loop of chenille.
Wrap the body and palmer the hackle; trim it short.
Tie in the turkey wings.
Wind the collar hackles and whip finish.

new.name: Letort Hopper
new.description: A low-floating hopper: yellow dubbed body, a turkey wing and a spun deer hair collar and head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on spring creeks to bank-feeding trout.
mats: Spun deer hair, tips as a collar
steps: Dub a slim body.
Tie a turkey wing flat on top.
Spin deer hair for the collar and head; trim the head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Letort Cricket
new.description: The Letort Hopper in black: black body, black crow or turkey wing and a black deer hair head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it close to the bank on spring creeks.
steps: Dub the body.
Tie the wing flat.
Spin and trim the black head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Schroeder's Parachute Hopper
new.description: A low-riding parachute hopper: tan body, turkey wing, white calf post and grizzly parachute hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Easy to see and floats low like a struggling hopper.
steps: Tie in the post.
Dub the body.
Tie the turkey wing low.
Wind the parachute hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Japanese Beetle
new.description: A shiny green-black foam beetle with a peacock body and legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it under trees in midsummer on eastern streams.
steps: Tie in the foam and wind herl.
Pull the foam over and tie it down.
Add the legs and whip finish.

new.name: Foam Cricket
new.description: A black foam cricket with black legs and a black wing.
new.fishing_tips: Splat it near banks in late summer.
steps: Lash the foam down in segments.
Add the wing.
Add the legs and whip finish.

new.name: Cicada
new.description: A big foam cicada with a black body, orange or tan wings and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it hard to the bank during cicada years.
mats: Synthetic wing film or elk hair
steps: Lash the foam body down.
Tie in the wing.
Add legs and eyes and whip finish.

new.name: Inchworm
new.description: A bright green chenille or foam caterpillar.
new.fishing_tips: Drift it under overhanging trees in late spring.
steps: Tie in the chenille.
Wrap or extend it along the shank.
Whip finish.

new.name: Green Weenie
new.description: A chartreuse chenille loop tail and body: an inchworm suggestion that catches fish all year.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it under an indicator.
mats: Chartreuse chenille with a loop tail
steps: Tie in the chenille with a short loop sticking past the bend.
Wrap it forward.
Whip finish.

new.name: Elk Hair Hopper
new.description: A deer or elk hair hopper with a dubbed body, elk wing and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it along grassy banks.
mats: Tan dubbing palmered with brown hackle
steps: Dub the body and palmer a hackle.
Tie in the elk wing and trim the butts as a head.
Add legs and whip finish.

new.name: Yellow Stimulator
new.description: The Stimulator in yellow: elk tail, yellow body palmered with grizzly, elk wing and an amber thorax with grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A Yellow Sally and golden stone suggestion; a top attractor.
steps: Tie in the tail and body hackle.
Dub the body and palmer the hackle.
Tie in the elk wing.
Dub the thorax and wind the front hackle through it.

new.name: Orange Stimulator
new.description: The Stimulator in orange for salmonflies and October caddis.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in pocket water during big stonefly and October caddis hatches.
steps: Tie in the tail and body hackle.
Dub the body and palmer.
Tie the wing.
Dub the thorax, wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Clark's Stonefly
new.description: A salmonfly dry with a flat gold tinsel body, orange and rust poly yarn wing over deer hair and a brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during the salmonfly hatch on western rivers.
mats: Orange and rust poly yarn, combed
steps: Wrap a gold tinsel body.
Tie in combed poly yarn.
Tie a deer hair wing over it.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Sofa Pillow
new.description: A classic salmonfly dry: red tail, orange floss body, red squirrel tail wing and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in heavy water during the salmonfly hatch.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the floss body.
Tie in the wing.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Bird's Stonefly
new.description: A big salmonfly dry: orange body palmered with trimmed hackle, deer hair wing, goose biot tails and antennae.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during the salmonfly hatch.
mats: Orange dubbing palmered with trimmed brown hackle
steps: Tie in the biot tails.
Dub and palmer the body, trimming the hackle short.
Tie in the deer hair wing.
Add the front hackle and antennae, whip finish.

new.name: Girdle Bug
new.description: A black chenille body with white rubber legs: the original rubber-leg stonefly.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it deep.
steps: Weight the hook.
Tie in legs at the tail, middle and front.
Wrap chenille between them and whip finish.

new.name: Twenty Incher
new.description: A peacock and pheasant tail stonefly nymph with a flashback wing case and hen hackle legs.
new.fishing_tips: A searching nymph for big trout.
mats: Pheasant tail with a peacock underbody
steps: Add the bead and tie in split biot tails.
Wrap the abdomen and rib it.
Tie in the wing case, wrap the thorax and add hen legs.
Pull the wing case over and whip finish.

new.name: Yuk Bug
new.description: A furry stonefly: grizzly hackle palmered through a black chenille body with white rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in fast water.
steps: Weight the hook and tie in the tail.
Tie in the legs and hackle.
Wrap the chenille and palmer the hackle.
Whip finish.

new.name: Golden Stonefly Dry
new.description: A big golden stone dry with an elk wing, a yellow-gold body and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during golden stone hatches in early summer.
steps: Tie in the tail and body hackle.
Dub and palmer the body.
Tie in the wing.
Wind the front hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Little Yellow Stone
new.description: A small yellow stonefly dry with a red butt, yellow body and a light elk wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in summer evenings when Yellow Sallies are laying eggs.
steps: Make a small red butt.
Dub the yellow body.
Tie in the wing.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Little Black Stone
new.description: A small black stonefly dry with a dark wing, for the first hatches of the year.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on late-winter and early-spring afternoons.
steps: Dub a slim body.
Tie in a downwing.
Wind a few turns of hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Brown Drake
new.description: A big dun for the brown drake hatch: a moose tail, a yellow-brown extended or dubbed body, deer hair wing and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Be on the water at dusk in early June when brown drakes hatch.
steps: Tie in the wing.
Tie in the tail.
Dub and rib the body.
Wind the hackles and whip finish.

new.name: Hex

new.description: A rabbit-tailed toad fly with a chenille head and lead eyes for redfish.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly near tailing redfish.
steps: Tie on the eyes and the tail.
Wrap the chenille head and trim it flat.

new.name: Ultra Shrimp
new.description: A translucent shrimp: a wrapped body of synthetic hair coated with epoxy and eyes made of burnt mono.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it near docks and flats.
steps: Tie in the antennae and eyes at the bend.
Build the body from synthetic hair.
Coat and shape it with epoxy.

new.name: Muddy Buddy
new.description: A deer hair head and a weighted body make the fly kick up mud like a feeding fish.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it on mud flats for redfish.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Add the tail.
Spin a deer hair head and trim it.

new.name: Toad Fly
new.description: A simple tarpon fly with a rabbit tail and a wrapped chenille head.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it in front of rolling tarpon.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Add the eyes and wrap the chenille head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Puglisi Peanut Butter
new.description: A small EP fibre baitfish with a slim profile for skinny water and small bait.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for snook, redfish and stripers.
steps: Tie in small bunches of EP fibres along the shank.
Trim to a slim baitfish shape.
Glue on the eyes.

new.name: EP Mullet
new.description: A big-headed mullet imitation of layered EP fibres.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it for snook, tarpon and redfish around mullet schools.
mats: EP fibres in grey, white and tan
steps: Tie EP fibres in bunches, fuller toward the head.
Trim to a blunt-headed mullet shape.
Glue on the eyes.

new.name: EP Baitfish
new.description: The classic EP baitfish: layered synthetic fibres trimmed into a tapered shape.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it wherever baitfish are about.
steps: Tie EP fibres in bunches along the shank.
Trim to a tapered baitfish.
Add eyes.

new.name: Flatwing
new.description: A long saddle hackle tied flat for a slim, undulating sand eel profile, with a bucktail support.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it slowly in current at night for stripers.
steps: Tie a sparse bucktail support with flash.
Tie a long saddle flat on top.
Add a peacock topping and eyes.

new.name: Glass Minnow
new.description: A tiny translucent baitfish of pearl body and sparse synthetic wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for snook, ladyfish and tarpon on small bait.
steps: Wrap a pearl body.
Tie in a sparse wing.
Add eyes and coat the head.

new.name: Tarpon Bunny
new.description: A rabbit strip tail and a palmered rabbit or hackle collar on a strong hook.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly ahead of tarpon.
steps: Tie in the rabbit tail.
Wrap a rabbit collar.
Whip finish.

new.name: Crease Fly
new.description: A foam sheet folded over the hook into a creased popper shape, coloured with markers.
new.fishing_tips: Pop it for stripers, bluefish and false albacore.
steps: Tie a bucktail tail.
Cut and fold the foam over the shank and glue it.
Colour it and add eyes.

new.name: Mylar Minnow
new.description: Mylar tubing slid over the shank with a bucktail or synthetic tail, coated with resin.
new.fishing_tips: Fast strips for mackerel and bluefish.
steps: Slide Mylar tubing over the shank and tie it down at both ends.
Unravel the tail end.
Add eyes and coat.

new.name: Sand Eel
new.description: A long, slim fly of sparse synthetic hair or bucktail for sand eels.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for stripers on sandy beaches.
steps: Wrap a pearl body.
Tie a long, sparse wing.
Add eyes and coat the head.

new.name: Bucktail Deceiver
new.description: A Deceiver built with a bucktail tail and collar instead of saddle hackles.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for stripers and snook.
steps: Tie a long bucktail tail.
Tie a bucktail collar all round the shank.
Add a darker top and eyes.

new.name: Hollow Deceiver
new.description: A Deceiver with hollow-tied bucktail at the head for bulk without weight.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for big stripers.
steps: Tie a saddle hackle tail.
Hollow-tie bucktail at the head.
Add eyes.

new.name: Bunker Fly
new.description: A big, deep-bodied menhaden imitation made of layered hollow-tied fibres with a dark spot behind the gill.
new.fishing_tips: Throw it on a heavy rod around bunker schools.
mats: Hollow-tied synthetic or bucktail, deep profile
steps: Hollow-tie long fibres in several bunches.
Build a deep body near the head.
Trim, add the spot and eyes.

new.name: Cobia Fly
new.description: A big, bright eel or baitfish fly with a long tail and a weighted head.
new.fishing_tips: Cast it ahead of cruising cobia.
steps: Tie on the eyes and a long tail.
Build the body.
Whip finish.

new.name: Deer Hair Mouse
new.description: A spun and trimmed deer hair mouse with a leather or rabbit tail and whiskers.
new.fishing_tips: Swim it across pools at night for big trout and bass.
mats: Spun deer hair, trimmed to a mouse
steps: Tie in the tail.
Spin and pack deer hair along the shank.
Trim to a mouse shape, flat underneath.
Add ears, whiskers and eyes.

new.name: Mr. Hankey
new.description: A deer hair and foam mouse with a rabbit tail, made famous on Alaskan and New Zealand rivers.
new.fishing_tips: Wake it across the current at dusk.
mats: Spun deer hair over a foam back
steps: Tie in the tail.
Spin and trim the hair body.
Add the foam back and whiskers.

new.name: Morrish Mouse
new.description: A foam-backed mouse with a deer hair head and a rabbit tail; floats low and wakes well.
new.fishing_tips: Swing and strip it at night.
steps: Tie in the tail and foam.
Wrap a rabbit body and pull the foam over.
Spin a deer hair head and add whiskers.

new.name: Mouse Rat
new.description: A rabbit-strip mouse with a foam back and a trimmed deer hair head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it at night along banks.
steps: Tie in the tail and foam.
Wrap the rabbit body.
Pull the foam over and add a hair head.

new.name: Frog Popper
new.description: A green and yellow foam or cork popper with rubber legs and a frog-like paint scheme.
new.fishing_tips: Pop it along lily pads.
mats: Foam or cork popper head, painted green
steps: Tie a marabou and hackle tail.
Glue on the popper head.
Add legs, eyes and paint.

new.name: Deer Hair Frog
new.description: A spun and trimmed deer hair frog with jointed back legs.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it among weeds and lily pads.
mats: Knotted deer hair or rubber legs
Spun deer hair in green, yellow and white bands, trimmed
steps: Tie in the back legs.
Spin coloured deer hair in bands.
Trim to a frog shape and add eyes and a weed guard.

new.name: Bluegill Popper
new.description: A small foam or cork popper with rubber legs for panfish.
new.fishing_tips: Pop it near beds in early summer.
steps: Tie a short marabou tail.
Glue on the popper head.
Push legs through the body.

new.name: Clouser Crayfish
new.description: Clouser's crayfish: a weighted, flat-bodied craw with mottled hen claws and a turkey shell.
new.fishing_tips: Hop it along rocky bottoms for smallmouth.
steps: Weight and flatten the shank.
Tie in the antennae and claws.
Dub and palmer the body, pull the shell over and segment it.
Coat the shell.

new.name: Wiggle Minnow
new.description: A foam-bodied minnow on an articulated tail hook that wiggles and dives on the strip.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it for bass and pike over weeds.
steps: Attach the foam body to the front shank.
Join the trailing hook with a tail.
Add eyes and coat.

new.name: Craw Daddy
new.description: A rabbit-claw crayfish with dumbbell eyes that rides hook-up.
new.fishing_tips: Crawl it along the bottom for bass and carp.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Tie in the claws.
Dub the body with legs and whip finish.

new.name: Hellgrammite
new.description: A big, dark dobsonfly larva with a marabou tail, chenille body and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift or crawl it in riffles for smallmouth.
mats: Black chenille, palmered with black hackle
steps: Weight the hook.
Tie in the tail and legs.
Wrap the body and palmer the hackle.
Add biot pincers.

new.name: Bunny Bug
new.description: A rabbit strip tail with a spun deer hair collar; simple and lively.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it for bass.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Spin and trim the head.

new.name: Hybrid Carp Fly
new.description: A small, weighted, buggy fly that hops along the bottom: suggests nymphs and crayfish.
new.fishing_tips: Cast it in front of feeding carp and twitch it.
steps: Tie on the eyes so the fly rides hook-up.
Add the tail and legs.
Dub the body.

new.name: Backstabber
new.description: A weighted carp fly with a marabou tail, a palmered body and rubber legs.
new.fishing_tips: Drop it in a feeding carp's path.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Add the tail.
Dub and palmer the body, add legs.

new.name: Headstand
new.description: A carp fly with heavy eyes at the front so it stands on its head on the bottom, tail waving.
new.fishing_tips: Let it sit near tailing carp.
steps: Tie heavy eyes at the front.
Tie in the tail and dub the body.

new.name: Duracell Jig
new.description: A tungsten jig nymph with a pheasant tail body, wire rib and a hot orange collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a Euro rig in riffles.
steps: Add the bead and a sparse tail.
Wrap and rib the body.
Dub a hot orange collar and whip finish.

new.name: Hare's Ear Jig
new.description: A jig-hook hare's ear with a tungsten bead and a buggy dubbed body.
new.fishing_tips: A great point fly on a Euro rig.
steps: Add the bead and tail.
Dub the body and rib it.
Pick it out and whip finish.

new.name: Pheasant Tail Jig
new.description: A jig pheasant tail with a tungsten bead and a hot-spot collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in pocket water.
steps: Add the bead and tail.
Wrap and rib the body.
Dub a collar and whip finish.

new.name: Tungsten Torpedo
new.description: A slim, heavy nymph with a thread body, pearl rib and a big tungsten bead.
new.fishing_tips: Get it down fast in heavy water.
steps: Add the bead and tail.
Wrap a slim body and rib it.
Coat it and add a small collar.

new.name: Blowtorch
new.description: A dark jig nymph with a pearl tinsel body, CDC collar and a fluorescent orange hot spot.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a Euro point fly.
steps: Add the bead and tail.
Wrap a tinsel body.
Wind a CDC collar and finish with an orange hot spot.

new.name: Tag Jig
new.description: A simple jig with a fluorescent tag, a peacock or dubbed body and a tungsten bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for trout and grayling on a Euro rig.
steps: Add the bead and tie a short tag.
Wrap the body and whip finish.

new.name: CDC Pheasant Tail
new.description: A beaded pheasant tail with a CDC collar that pulses in the current.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it under an indicator or on a Euro rig.
steps: Add the bead and tail.
Wrap and rib the body.
Wind a CDC collar and whip finish.

new.name: Ice Cream Cone
new.description: A chironomid pupa with a black thread body, wire rib and a white bead and gills.
new.fishing_tips: Hang it under an indicator near the bottom in lakes.
steps: Add the bead.
Wrap a tapered thread body and rib it.
Add a small white gill tuft and whip finish.

new.name: Chironomid Pupa
new.description: A thin, segmented thread body with a wire rib, thorax and white gills.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly under an indicator.
steps: Wrap a slim body and rib it.
Wrap a thorax and add gills.
Whip finish.

new.name: Snow Cone
new.description: A black chironomid with a white bead, a red wire rib and a coated body.
new.fishing_tips: Hang it deep in lakes.
steps: Add the bead.
Wrap and rib the body.
Coat it and whip finish.

new.name: Bomber Chironomid
new.description: A bigger chironomid with a stripped quill or tinsel body and a peacock thorax with white gills.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it under an indicator during big chironomid hatches.
steps: Wrap the body.
Add the thorax and gills.
Whip finish.

new.name: Chromie
new.description: A silver tinsel chironomid with a black rib, a peacock thorax and a white bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it near the bottom in lakes.
steps: Add the bead.
Wrap the silver body and rib it.
Add a peacock thorax.

new.name: Dragonfly Nymph
new.description: A wide, buggy nymph with a fat abdomen, big eyes and legs.
new.fishing_tips: Crawl it slowly along the bottom in lakes.
steps: Tie in the eyes.
Dub a fat abdomen.
Add legs and wing case, dub the thorax.

new.name: Water Boatman
new.description: A small, oval bug with a shiny back and oar-like legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the shallows in late summer and autumn.
steps: Wrap the body.
Pull the back over.
Tie in biot legs each side.

new.name: Backswimmer
new.description: A foam-backed bug that swims upside down with long oar legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it near the surface with short pulls.
steps: Dub the body.
Pull the foam over.
Add the legs.

new.name: Doc Spratley
new.description: A BC lake classic: grizzly tail, black wool body ribbed with silver, grizzly throat and a pheasant tail wing over a peacock head.
new.fishing_tips: Troll or strip it slowly in lakes.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Wrap and rib the body.
Add the throat and wing, wind a peacock head.

new.name: Seal Bugger
new.description: A Woolly Bugger with a seal fur body: buggy and translucent.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly in lakes.
steps: Tie in the tail and hackle.
Dub the body.
Palmer the hackle forward.

new.name: Carey Special
new.description: A pheasant rump hackle over a peacock or wool body: a buggy lake fly.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly near weedbeds.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the body.
Wind the rump hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Tom Thumb
new.description: A deer hair fly whose tips form the tail and the wing, folded over a hair body.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it dry or skate it on lakes during sedge hatches.
steps: Tie in a bunch of deer hair with tips back as the tail.
Fold it forward over the shank and tie down, leaving tips up as a wing.

new.name: Mosquito Larva
new.description: A slim, segmented larva of stripped quill with a small thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it near the surface in still water.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the quill body.
Dub the thorax.

new.name: Green Highlander
new.description: A classic salmon fly: yellow and green body, gold tinsel rib, green hackle, yellow throat and a mixed wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for salmon; tied as a hairwing it fishes well too.
mats: Yellow floss rear, green seal front
Mixed fibres or green and yellow hair
steps: Tie the tag, tail and butt.
Wrap the two-part body and rib it, palmer the hackle over the front.
Add the throat.
Tie in the wing and whip finish.

new.name: Jock Scott
new.description: The most famous classic salmon fly: two-part yellow and black body, guinea throat and an elaborate wing (often tied as a hairwing today).
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for salmon in summer.
mats: Yellow floss rear, black floss front with veiling
Mixed fibres or a hair wing
steps: Tie the tag and tail.
Wrap the two-part body and rib it.
Add the throat.
Build the wing and cheeks.

new.name: Durham Ranger
new.description: An orange and claret-bodied classic with golden pheasant tippets in the wing and badger hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it in coloured water.
mats: Yellow, orange, claret and black seal fur
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub the banded body and rib it.
Palmer the hackle and add the throat.
Tie in the tippet wing.

new.name: Stoat's Tail
new.description: A simple black hairwing: black floss body, silver rib, black hackle and a black stoat or squirrel wing.
new.fishing_tips: A summer low-water salmon fly.
steps: Tie a silver tag.
Wrap and rib the black body.
Add the throat and wing.

new.name: Willie Gunn
new.description: A black-bodied tube or hairwing fly with a mixed yellow, orange and black wing.
new.fishing_tips: A top cold-water salmon fly.
mats: Yellow, orange and black bucktail, mixed
steps: Wrap and rib the body.
Tie a mixed hair wing in three colours.

new.name: Cascade
new.description: A shrimp-style salmon fly: long orange and yellow tail with flash, silver and black body and an orange and yellow hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Excellent in summer and autumn.
mats: Orange and yellow bucktail with flash
steps: Tie in the long tail.
Wrap the two-part body and rib it.
Wind the hackles and tie in the wing.

new.name: Sunray Shadow
new.description: A long-wing tube fly: white bucktail under a long black hair wing with peacock herl topping.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast across pools for salmon.
mats: Plastic or aluminium tube with a treble
White bucktail, then long black goat or squirrel
steps: Tie white hair under the tube.
Tie a long black wing on top.
Add peacock herl and whip finish.

new.name: Frances Fly
new.description: An Icelandic shrimp fly with long antennae, a ribbed body and a hackle shell.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it for salmon in Iceland and Scotland.
steps: Tie in the long antennae.
Wrap and rib the body.
Tie the shell over the back.

new.name: Collie Dog
new.description: A tube fly with a very long black wing of goat or collie hair over a silver body.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it across salmon pools.
steps: Wrap the body.
Tie in a long black wing.

new.name: Munro Killer
new.description: A black hairwing with a gold rib, orange and blue throat and black and yellow wing.
new.fishing_tips: A good salmon fly in peaty water.
steps: Wrap and rib the body.
Add the throat.
Tie the wing.

new.name: Silver Stoat
new.description: A Stoat's Tail with a silver body.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in bright conditions.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap and rib the silver body.
Add hackle and wing.

new.name: Hairy Mary
new.description: A black and gold hairwing with a blue throat and a brown wing.
new.fishing_tips: A summer salmon favourite.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Wrap the body.
Add the throat and wing.

new.name: General Practitioner
new.description: Drury's shrimp: golden pheasant tippet eyes, orange seal body palmered with orange hackle and a golden pheasant red breast back.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for salmon in autumn.
mats: Orange seal fur palmered with orange hackle
steps: Tie in the whiskers and tippet eyes.
Dub and palmer the body in sections, tying in back feathers as you go.
Rib it and whip finish.

new.name: Intruder
new.description: A big, light steelhead fly on a shank: a trailing hook, a rear hackle hub and long front collars of ostrich, marabou and flash.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on sink-tips for winter steelhead.
steps: Attach the trailing hook loop.
Build a rear dubbing hub and wind a hackle.
Wind ostrich and marabou collars with flash at the front.
Whip finish.

new.name: Buck Bug
new.description: A palmered deer hair-tailed bug with a green or orange butt, fished dry or wet for Atlantic salmon.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift or swing it on the Miramichi.
mats: Spun deer hair, trimmed, palmered with brown hackle
steps: Tie in the tail and butt.
Spin and trim the body.
Palmer the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Squidro
new.description: A squid-like Intruder variant with long legs and a big collar.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for steelhead and salmon.
steps: Attach the trailing hook.
Tie in the tentacles.
Wind a marabou collar.

new.name: Signature Intruder
new.description: Ed Ward's signature Intruder with layered ostrich, flash and rhea collars.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on big rivers.
steps: Build the rear hub.
Wind rear and front collars.
Finish the head.

new.name: Freight Train
new.description: A banded steelhead fly with a purple, orange and red body under a white wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for summer steelhead.
mats: Flat silver, red and orange floss, black chenille
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wrap the banded body.
Add hackle and wing.

new.name: Purple Peril
new.description: A purple-bodied steelhead classic with a silver rib and a brown or purple wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for summer steelhead.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Wrap and rib the body.
Add the hackle and wing.

new.name: Moal Leech
new.description: A rabbit strip steelhead leech with a long tail and a palmered collar.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it slowly in cold water.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Palmer the rabbit strip forward.
Wind a schlappen collar.

new.name: String Leech
new.description: A long, slim leech of rabbit strip on a shank with a trailing hook.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on a sink-tip.
steps: Attach the trailer.
Tie in the long tail.
Wind a marabou collar.

new.name: Prom Dress
new.description: A bright pink and orange Intruder-style steelhead fly.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it in coloured water.
mats: Pink and orange marabou and ostrich
steps: Build the hub.
Wind the collars.
Whip finish.
